privacy.label: Legal
privacy.title: Privacy policy.
privacy.description: What SecureCargo collects, why, who processes it, how long it is kept and how to exercise your rights under the LGPD and the GDPR.
intro: This policy explains, in plain language, what SecureCargo does with personal data. It is written for Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018) and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and it describes what the system really does today.

sections.heading: Who we are
body: SecureCargo is run by Levi Braga, individual developer, Jundiaí, SP, Brazil, as a project for the Hack Brasil 2026 hackathon. For the personal data described here, Levi Braga is the controller (in the LGPD's words, the *controlador*).
To reach us about privacy, use the [contact form](/contact) and pick the subject **Privacy or data request**. The form is the only contact channel; we do not publish an email address.

sections.heading: What we collect

list: **Account:** your email address and name, your organization's name and type (insurer or carrier) and your role in it. Your password is handled by our sign-in provider, Clerk; we never see it. If a manager invites a colleague, we keep the invited email address until the invitation is used or expires.
**Demo visitors:** the demo buttons create no account. Your browser gets a random demo session and a sandbox, and nothing about you is asked.

**Inspections:** the photos of the load you take or upload (1 to 4), the truck you pick (body, size, dimensions, optional nickname in "My trucks"), the cargo weight, any notes, the readings and edits you confirm, the simulation results, the fix and the certificate. The plate field exists but is off unless your organization turns it on.
**Invoice photo:** if you choose "Read from invoice", we keep the photo of the invoice (DANFE) and the gross weight read from it. An invoice can show company names, tax numbers and addresses.

**Activity and usage:** an audit trail of each inspection (who created, edited, fixed or shared it, and when) and a record of each photo analysis (the AI model, the number of tokens and the estimated cost) to enforce quotas and the monthly budget.
**Contact form messages:** your name, the email address you want the reply sent to, the subject, the message, the page you wrote from, the site language and the date.
**IP address and technical data:** used for rate limits, anti-spam and abuse protection, and recorded for a short time in our providers' request logs. See "How long we keep data".
**Cookies and local storage:** listed on the [cookie page](/cookies).

body: We remove the location (GPS) and other metadata (EXIF) from every photo, first on your phone before it is sent and again on our server before it is stored. Please avoid photographing faces or readable plates: they are not needed for the check.

sections.heading: Why we use it, and the legal basis

list: **To provide the inspection service** (analysis, simulation, results, certificates, your organization's dashboard): performance of a contract (LGPD art. 7, V; GDPR art. 6(1)(b)).
**To keep the service secure and free of abuse** (sign-in, rate limits, Turnstile, audit trail): our legitimate interest (LGPD art. 7, IX; GDPR art. 6(1)(f)).
**To control costs** (quotas and the monthly budget for photo analysis): our legitimate interest in keeping a free service available.

**To answer your messages:** our legitimate interest in replying to you, or steps you asked for before a contract (LGPD art. 7, V and IX; GDPR art. 6(1)(b) and (f)). For privacy requests, also a legal obligation (LGPD art. 7, II; GDPR art. 6(1)(c)).
**Strictly necessary cookies:** they make sign-in and the demo work, so they need no consent.

body: We do not sell personal data, we do not use it for advertising, and we do not use it to train AI models. We do not make decisions about you based only on automated processing: a SecureCargo result is advice about a load, and the driver and the carrier decide.

sections.heading: When you use SecureCargo through your company
body: An insurer or a carrier can use SecureCargo for its drivers and inspectors. The organization's managers see every inspection of their organization, and they decide how those inspections are used. For that data we act on the organization's behalf, so some requests (for example, deleting an inspection your company must keep) may need to go through your company.

sections.heading: Who processes data for us
body: We use these service providers (processors, or *operadores* in the LGPD), each under its own data processing terms:

list: **Clerk** (United States): accounts, sign-in, organizations and invitations, and the sign-in emails. [Clerk privacy policy](https://clerk.com/legal/privacy)

**Cloudflare** (United States, global network): our API, the database (D1), the private photo storage (R2), the contact form's email (Email Service), Turnstile anti-spam and request logs. [Cloudflare privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) · [Turnstile privacy addendum](https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/)
**Vercel** (United States): hosts the website and keeps short request logs. [Vercel privacy policy](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy)

**Anthropic** (United States): the Claude model reads your load and invoice photos to suggest units, restraints and the gross weight. We use Anthropic's commercial API. Under its terms, Anthropic does not use API inputs or outputs to train its models by default, and deletes them within 30 days, except when it must keep them longer to enforce its usage policy or by law. [Is my data used for model training?](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training) · [How long Anthropic stores API data](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data) · [Anthropic commercial terms](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms)
**Google** (Gmail): the contact form's messages arrive in our mailbox there.

sections.heading: International transfers
body: These providers process data in the United States and in other countries where they operate, so your data leaves Brazil and, for European visitors, the European Economic Area. We rely on the safeguards in their data processing terms, such as standard contractual clauses (LGPD art. 33; GDPR art. 46) and, where a provider is certified, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (GDPR art. 45).

list: **Demo sessions:** everything a demo visitor creates is deleted automatically 24 hours after it was created. The demo session cookie also expires after 24 hours. The pre-made demo inspections use sample photos and fictitious names and are kept.

**Accounts:** until you delete the account. Inspections, photos, invoice photos, results, certificates, trucks, the audit trail and usage records are kept while the account exists. When you delete it (see "Your rights"), inspections you made outside an organization are deleted with their photos, invoice photos and stored results; inspections you made for an organization stay with it, for its records, with your name and email removed and an entry "author deleted their account" in their history; the cost records of your photo analyses stay without any link to you, for the monthly budget; your saved trucks, your membership and your sign-in at Clerk are deleted. A certificate's public verification page stops working when its inspection is deleted.
**Photo analysis cache:** the AI's reading of a photo is kept, keyed by the photo's fingerprint (SHA-256), so the same photo is never paid for twice. It describes cargo, not people.

**Contact form messages:** we do not store them in our database. They are only emailed to us, and we delete them from our mailbox within 90 days after the conversation ends, unless we need them to handle a legal claim.
**Contact form counter:** to limit each address to 5 messages an hour we keep a keyed hash (HMAC) of your IP address, never the address itself, for at most 2 hours.
**Request logs:** Cloudflare keeps the API's logs for up to 7 days and Vercel keeps the website's logs for up to 1 hour on our plan.
**At Anthropic:** up to 30 days, as described above.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask us to confirm whether we process your data; to access it; to correct it; to delete it; to receive a copy in a portable format (JSON); to know who we share it with; to object to processing based on legitimate interest; and to withdraw any consent you gave. You can also complain to Brazil's data protection authority, the [ANPD](https://www.gov.br/anpd), or, in the EU, to your local supervisory authority.

**How:** to delete your account, open the account menu (your picture at the top of the app), choose **Delete my account** and type the confirmation word; it takes effect at once. For anything else, send the request through the [contact form](/contact) with the subject **Privacy or data request**, writing from the email address of your account so we can confirm it is you. We answer within 15 days. You can correct your name and your inspections yourself in the app.

sections.heading: Security
body: All traffic uses HTTPS. Photos are kept in a private bucket and are only served to people allowed to see them; every request is checked on the server (a driver sees only their own inspections, a manager only their organization's). Passwords are handled by Clerk. API keys and other secrets live only in our providers' secret stores. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach puts you at risk, we will tell you and the authorities as the law requires.

sections.heading: Children
body: SecureCargo is meant for professional use and is not intended for anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from children.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
body: If we change what we collect or why, we will update this page and the date at its top.

terms.label: Legal
terms.title: Terms of use.
terms.description: The terms for using SecureCargo: a decision-support tool for cargo securement, not an engineering certification or legal advice.
intro: By using SecureCargo (the website at securecargo.app, the app and the API) you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use it.

sections.heading: What SecureCargo is
body: SecureCargo is operated by Levi Braga, individual developer, Jundiaí, SP, Brazil.

SecureCargo checks whether a truck's cargo is well distributed and properly secured, using a photo or the data you enter, a physics simulation and a set of road-transport rules (Brazil, the United States or the European Union). [How we calculate](/methodology) explains the model and its limits.

**SecureCargo is a decision-support tool.** It is not an engineering certification, an inspection by an authority, an insurance assessment or legal advice. A SecureCargo certificate records what the tool computed; it does not certify that a load complies with the law.

sections.heading: Your responsibility
body: The driver and the carrier remain responsible for securing the load under the law that applies to the trip (in Brazil, among others, the Brazilian Traffic Code and CONTRAN Resolutions 945/2022 and 882/2021). Always check the load yourself, follow the manufacturer's limits for straps, chains and anchor points, and re-tighten restraints during the trip.

sections.heading: Results depend on what you give us
body: A result is only as good as the photo and the data entered. The AI can miss or misread straps, units or weights; a weight marked "estimated" is a guess, not a measurement. Review what was read and correct it before relying on the result. The simulation models a rigid load on a flat bed and does not cover every real situation.

sections.heading: Acceptable use

list: Do not send spam, advertising or abusive messages through the contact form or any other feature.
Do not upload content you have no right to share, or photos of people's faces or readable plates.
Do not try to break, overload or get around the security, rate limits or quotas of the service, or access data that is not yours.
Do not use the service for anything illegal.

body: We may block an account or an address that breaks these rules.

sections.heading: Demo data resets
body: The demo buttons give anyone access without an account. Anything created in a demo session is deleted automatically after 24 hours, and the demo organization can be reset at any time. Do not put real or sensitive information into a demo session.

sections.heading: Hackathon project, no warranty
body: SecureCargo is a project built for the Hack Brasil 2026 hackathon and is in beta. It is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind, and it may change, stop working or be shut down without notice. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for losses that come from using it or relying on its results. Nothing in these terms limits rights that consumer law gives you and that cannot be waived.
The source code is open (MIT license) on [GitHub](https://github.com/levimbraga/secure-cargo).

sections.heading: Privacy
body: How we handle personal data is described in the [privacy policy](/privacy) and the [cookie page](/cookies).

sections.heading: Applicable law and changes
body: These terms are governed by Brazilian law. We may update them; the date at the top of this page shows the current version.

sections.heading: Contact
body: Questions about these terms: use the [contact form](/contact), the only contact channel.

methodology.label: Resources
methodology.title: How we calculate.
methodology.description: How SecureCargo decides whether a load arrives intact: the MuJoCo physics model, the trip events, the verdict thresholds and the validation against EN 12195-1.
intro: SecureCargo's verdict comes from a physics simulation, not from a rule of thumb. This page explains the model in plain words and shows that, wherever a closed-form calculation exists, the simulation gives the same answer. The full technical documents are on GitHub: [physics model](https://github.com/levimbraga/secure-cargo/blob/main/docs/physics-model.md) and [validation](https://github.com/levimbraga/secure-cargo/blob/main/docs/validation.md).

list: **Perceive.** From a photo (read by the Claude vision model, then confirmed or corrected by the driver) or from the manual editor, we get the truck, each cargo unit (size, weight, position) and the restraints in place. The AI never invents weights: they come from the total you enter or from the invoice.

**Simulate.** The MuJoCo physics engine puts the truck bed through seven trip situations: emergency braking, a lane change, a sharp curve, a pothole, a speed bump, a long descent and long vibration. It records what slides, tips, rolls, hits the headboard or overloads a strap.

**Plan.** If something fails, the planner tries the cheapest changes first (move units, add straps, an anti-slip mat, diagonals, edge protectors), keeps only the ones that are needed, and proves the fixed load in the same seven situations.
**Check the rules.** Separately, the load is checked against the securing, weight and dimension rules of Brazil, the United States or the European Union. See [rule sources](/rules).

The **truck bed** is a body whose motion is prescribed: it follows the acceleration of each trip event within a micrometre. The truck itself does not roll, pitch or yaw, and its suspension is not modelled.
**Cargo units** are rigid boxes or cylinders (coils, drums, pipes) with their weight, standing on the floor or on each other. Friction between each pair of materials comes from the EN 12195-1 table.

**Straps, chains and ropes** are tension-only springs with a pretension, a working capacity (LC) and a stretch. A top-over strap only presses the load down and holds by friction, exactly as the standard assumes. A diagonal (direct) lashing pulls on a fixed point.

**Walls and blocks** (headboard, side walls, chocks, coil cradles) only push. The front wall of a box truck or curtain-sider is taken as an EN 12642 code L wall (0.4 × payload, at most 5,000 daN); a curtain-sider's curtains restrain nothing.
Every run uses a fixed 2 ms time step and no randomness: the same input always gives the same output.

sections.heading: Trip conditions
body: Speed (20 to 100 km/h), road type and weather change the events. A wet road lowers how hard the truck can brake, but not the friction between cargo and a clean deck; mud and gravel do, because the deck is no longer clean. Fog means a later, harsher braking. Every number has a source or is labelled as an assumption in the [physics model](https://github.com/levimbraga/secure-cargo/blob/main/docs/physics-model.md):

head: Quantity
Value
Source
rows: EN 12195-1; Wong, Theory of Ground Vehicles

sections.heading: From simulation to verdict
body: The standard designs for no movement. Our thresholds separate real movement from elastic give:

head: What is measured
Warning
Fail
rows: above its capacity, or it broke
Unit left the bed or hit the headboard

body: The result has three states, the same everywhere: **Approved** (every situation holds and every rule passes), **Holds, but out of compliance** (the physics holds but a rule fails, for example an axle over its limit) and **Does not arrive intact** (a unit slides, tips, rolls, hits the headboard or breaks a lashing in at least one situation).

sections.heading: Validation against EN 12195-1
body: EN 12195-1 is the European standard for calculating cargo-securing forces. On the cases where it has a formula, we ran the simulation and compared. Every number below is asserted by an automated test that runs on every change.

head: Check
Formula
Simulation
Difference
rows: Pallet with 2 straps: braking at which it slides
Crate with 4 straps: braking at which it slides
Unsecured box: braking at which it slides
Unsecured 0.8 × 2.0 m box: braking at which it tips
Tension in two direct lashings, 3 t box at 0.8 g
Force on the headboard, 2 t box at 0.8 g

Coil rolling over a 15 cm chock

body: In five lashing cases the simulation fails with one strap fewer than the formula asks for and passes with the formula's number, and the load does not move at all in the passing runs. The fixed demo scenarios carry what the standard asks for **with** its safety factor (1.25 forward), so they pass with margin.

sections.heading: Live in your browser, certified on the server
body: The live lab runs the same MuJoCo model in your browser through WebAssembly. The server sends the exact model it simulates, and on the eight demo runs the browser and the server agree to the tenth of a millimetre and the newton. Browser results are labelled "live, not certified": certificates only ever use the server's result.

list: The simulation is validated against the standard's own model of a rigid load on a flat floor. It has not been compared with physical crash or braking tests.
Friction factors come from the standard's table. A real deck that is oily, icy or worn has less.
Units are rigid, with the centre of gravity in the middle; a strap over a stack is attached to the top unit.
The photo reading can miss or misread straps and units. Review it before relying on the result.
**SecureCargo is a decision-support tool, not an engineering certification.**

sections.heading: A note on accuracy
body: We check rules from the official texts and test each one with a passing and a failing case, but laws change and interpretations differ. SecureCargo is a decision-support tool, not legal advice. If you find a rule we got wrong, tell us through the [contact form](/contact) with the subject **Report a problem**.
